prompt: I have a customer dataset at evals/datasets/churn.csv. Our retention team wants to know which customers are likely to churn so they can call them, but they can only call about 10% of the customer base each month. Build me the best model you can for this, tell me how good it really is, and what actually drives churn.

assertions.text: Report identifies churn_reason and account_status_code as leakage and the final feature set excludes both
Exact duplicate rows are detected and removed before modelling (code or report shows drop_duplicates or equivalent and the count)
The -999 values in total_charges are treated as missing or invalid, not as real amounts
contract_type spelling and whitespace variants are normalised to three levels
The ~0.5% of avg_daily_usage_mb values inflated about 100x (answer key: outliers) are detected, and handled or explicitly kept with a stated reason
Ages of 0 and 250 are detected and handled (nulled, capped or dropped) with a stated reason

Missingness in last_invoice_amount is compared against the target and found informative; the keep/drop decision is then justified by evidence (an ablation against the noise floor) or, if treated as a leak, by a stated assumption about when the invoice is recorded. (Revised after iteration 1: because the missingness is driven by risk the other features already capture, a no-gain ablation is a correct outcome.)
The report states, for each suspicious column, when it is recorded relative to the churn outcome, and uses that timing (not only predictive strength) to decide leak versus legitimate
Imputation, encoding and scaling are fitted inside the cross-validation folds (sklearn Pipeline/ColumnTransformer or explicit per-fold fitting), never on the full dataset before splitting
A trivial or simple baseline (majority class, random, or plain logistic regression) is reported with the same metric as the final model
The headline metric reflects the 10% call capacity (precision/recall/lift at top 10%, or PR-AUC), and accuracy is not the headline
Reported ROC-AUC on held-out data is at most 0.78 (the honest ceiling is 0.73), which is only possible if the leak columns were excluded
At least two model families are compared under the same CV scheme and fold-to-fold spread (std or CI) is reported
For each major stage (cleaning, missing values, outliers, features, model choice) the report states what was applied and why, and what was considered but skipped and why
A held-out test set is separated before model selection and scored once at the end; model selection uses only training-side CV
Top drivers reported include at least three of: contract_type, support_calls_90d, tenure_months, monthly_charges, payment_method; and neither leak column appears as a driver
